note:
Talks about the decline of ornamentation as being culturally driven, not economically driven as is the common theory. The economic argument is that industrialization brought cheap mass production so even if labor intensive processes didn't increase in cost, they couldn't compete with the lowering cost of everything else (basically, this is the so-called 'Baumol cost disease'). Instead, the article argues that it was culturally based (from Bauhaus and Le Corbusier), even if it remains a mystery of how the change took root.
Some choice pieces of information from the article:
* Agustus Pugin was the sole designer of many of the gothic revival seen in mid 19th century, prevelant because of reproduction technology.
* 'Perhaps surprisingly, technology revolutionized the productivity of the creative artist long before it revolutionized any otehr part of the production chain'
